purpose: Formal pruning and debloat policy for CYNIC crates, modules, and dependency boundaries. Behavior-driven, auditable, revocable.

excludes: isolated experimental fragments unless promoted into the workspace

module_sufficient.description: A module is enough when the boundary is only organizational or narrative, with no independent compilation, reuse, versioning, or test/service reason.
module_sufficient.note: crate splitting is not a goal in itself

conditions: A responsibility changes on a different schedule or reason
A distinct compilation/service requirement (build, runtime, no_std, wasm, isolated test, feature gating, heavy dependency isolation)
A stable public API that is reused, or must be reused
A dependency cycle that forces moving a shared responsibility into a separate crate or shared abstraction

suspect_over_splitting.signal: A crate is too small, too tightly coupled to one consumer, and has no strong reason to live on its own.
suspect_over_splitting.action: Candidate for fusion or return to a module, not yet another crate.

responsibility_rules.clear_owner: Each crate/module must have an identifiable perimeter and a clear contract for what it exposes vs hides.
responsibility_rules.public_surface_contract: Public surface is a commitment; it does not expand without reason.
responsibility_rules.one_way_dependency: Dependency direction must be readable; obscure, implicit, or bidirectional dependencies are avoided without an abstraction.
responsibility_rules.domain_no_infrastructure_by_default: Domain logic must not depend on adapters, infrastructure, framework, driver, or runtime-specific concerns unless it is explicitly that kind of layer.

visibility_rules.tightest_usable: Use the narrowest visibility that communicates intent. Private by default, pub(crate) for internal shared detail, pub only where it is a real public API.
visibility_rules.no_permanent_broadening: Do not keep a module or item permanently over-opened for a temporary convenience. If opened, document why and close it again when possible.

pruning_rules.remove_orphans_first: Orphaned, abandoned, or non-verified modules/crates with no real reason are removal or fusion candidates, before structural design.
pruning_rules.no_footprint_justification: Do not keep code 'just in case' without a current reason. A pure future justification without a present trigger is archived or isolated, not kept as passive debt.
pruning_rules.extract_only_with_real_reason: Before extracting a crate, verify the reason for the crate is real and current. A hypothetical future reason is delayed or documented with a trigger, not used to force a new crate now.
pruning_rules.no_split_for_split_sake: Do not fragment into more crates to satisfy an empty formal rule.

debt_and_cleanup_rules.debt_as_state: Treat debt as a measurable, owned state, not vague discomfort. 'Old' is not enough by itself.
debt_and_cleanup_rules.deduplication_before_new_abstraction: Merge proven duplication before introducing new abstractions.
debt_and_cleanup_rules.refactor_for_reason: Refactor from an identified problem, with a proposed fix, verified effects, and only the necessary moves.

maintenance_rules.verify_before_touching: Verify users, dependencies, tests, references, build effects, and runtime impact before touching a module or crate.
maintenance_rules.no_refactor_by_default: Refactor from a real identified problem, not from a desire to move code for its own sake.

violations.god_module: One module or crate accumulating unrelated responsibilities with no clear boundary is a violation signal, not yet a verdict.
violations.dumping_ground: A module that becomes a catch-all without a coherent responsibility is a violation signal.
violations.framework_in_domain: Domain code importing framework, driver, runtime, or infrastructure-specific types without an explicit adapter role is a violation signal.
violations.broad_pub_by_convenience: Permanent over-broad visibility used to avoid a real boundary is a violation signal.

known_ambiguities.suspect_to_small_crate_threshold: The exact threshold for 'too small a crate' is contextual; the rule gives a signal, not an automatic verdict.
known_ambiguities.module_vs_crate_elasticity: The line can shift over time when a reason becomes real or disappears.

known_exclusions: This policy does not replace verification of code, tests, dependencies, build, and real impact.
This policy does not decide automatically; it produces signals and decision rules.

ratification.why: This policy was used as the decision rule for the whole crate fusion programme — infra/CRATE_FUSION_DISPOSITIONS.md applies crate_justified and suspect_over_splitting to 10 candidates, and those dispositions are only proposals rather than opinions because the rule they were derived from is now authority. A contract left in draft while being used to rule is the same failure as a denylist nobody compares: it looks like a policy and decides nothing.
ratification.applies_to_the_agent: This policy is the authority for whether a crate may be created, fused, or removed. It is machine-checked in part by ARCH-004 in cynic-host::audit_engine, which enforces the justification clause against the observed manifests, and the remainder is carried by infra/CRATE_FUSION_DISPOSITIONS.md, whose lists may only shrink.
